questions.q: Why were Christmas and New Year no holiday for cabmen?
choices: So many parties meant hard work, often very late
All the cabs in London were closed for the holidays
The horses had to stay home in their stables
No one wanted to ride in cabs in the cold
questions.evidence: There are so many parties, balls, and places of amusement open that the work is hard and often late

questions.q: Why did Jack do most of the evening work?
choices: He was used to standing, and Hotspur might catch cold
Hotspur was lame from a stone in his shoe
Jack was the younger and stronger horse
Hotspur would not work at night in the dark
questions.evidence: I was well accustomed to standing, and Jerry was also more afraid of Hotspur taking cold

questions.q: What time were Jerry and Jack told to come back for the two gentlemen?
choices: Eleven o'clock
Nine o'clock
Midnight
Two in the morning
questions.evidence: were told to come again at eleven

questions.q: What was the weather like while Jerry waited outside?
choices: Sharp, driving sleet with no shelter
Warm and still, like a summer night
Light snow falling with a clear sky
Thick yellow fog but no wind or rain at all
questions.evidence: now it came on sharp, driving sleet

questions.q: When did the two gentlemen finally come out?
choices: At a quarter past one
Right at eleven o'clock
At half-past eleven
At six in the morning
questions.evidence: At a quarter past one the door opened

questions.q: How did the gentlemen behave about keeping Jerry waiting so long?
choices: They never said sorry and were angry at the charge
They apologized and paid him extra for waiting
They gave Jerry a warm coat to wear home
They invited him inside to warm up by the fire
questions.evidence: they never said they were sorry to have kept us waiting so long, but were angry at the charge

questions.q: What did Jerry do for Jack when they got home, even though he was very ill?
choices: Rubbed him down and gave him extra straw
Left him in his harness all night long
Sent him to a neighbor's stable for the night
Went straight to bed without seeing him
questions.evidence: he gave me a rub-down as usual, and even went up into the hayloft for an extra bundle of straw for my bed

questions.q: Harry "was very still, and neither whistled nor sang" the next morning. What does this tell you?
choices: He was worried because his father was very ill
He had a sore throat from the cold night air
He was angry at the two gentlemen who kept them waiting
He was too sleepy to sing after a late night
questions.evidence: He was very still, and neither whistled nor sang

questions.q: Harry says, "they call it 'bronchitis'." From the chapter, what is bronchitis?
choices: A serious illness of the chest and breathing
A broken bone in the arm or leg
A kind of medicine the farrier gives sick horses
A red, itchy rash on the skin

questions.q: Why did the doctor say Jerry had a better chance than most men?
choices: Because he didn't drink
Because he was very young
Because he was rich
Because he lived in the country
questions.evidence: father had a better chance than most men, because he didn't drink

questions.q: How did Governor Grant help the family while Jerry was sick?
choices: He worked Hotspur and gave Polly half the money
He paid the whole of the doctor's bill himself
He bought Jack from Polly for a good price
He drove Jerry to the hospital every day
questions.evidence: whatever he earns, I'll bring your mother half of it

questions.q: What did the doctor say Jerry must never do again?
choices: Go back to the cab work
Ride or drive a horse
Live anywhere in London
Eat meat or drink coffee
questions.evidence: he must never go back to the cab work again if he wished to be an old man

questions.q: What did Mrs. Fowler's letter offer the family?
choices: A cottage near her and a coachman's job for Jerry
A large sum of money to pay the doctor
A new cab and two young horses to start afresh
Tickets for the whole family to travel abroad for his health
questions.evidence: Mrs. Fowler says we are all to go and live near her

questions.q: Why was the family's good news "heavy news" for Black Beauty?
choices: He would be sold and lose his best master since Birtwick
He had to pull the heavy moving cart to the country
He would have to share a stall with Hotspur
He did not like the country and wanted to stay
questions.evidence: Since I left Birtwick I had never been so happy as with my dear master Jerry
